ladders.cameras: about 2,000 readers from three vendors, of which 138 Flock poles
ladders.note: Inspector General review. False alerts were traced to stale or wrong database entries rather than misreads. The department suspended the Flock contract in July 2026.

Alerts include more than 620,000 for stolen plates; the department kept stolen-vehicle alerts deactivated for staffing reasons. Recoveries and arrests are the 425 outcomes officers logged in the software's outcome feature, not a count of all alerts.

ladders.cameras: 42 fixed Flock cameras; 50 patrol cars with in-car readers
ladders.note: Alerts are 1,748 on official lists plus 18,638 on agency custom lists. Reads cover the only 38-day window the system still held; purge data for 2025 was unavailable. 49 investigations used reader data. Shares camera access with 299 agencies.

Alerts on stolen-vehicle and felony lists; 71% involved a misread plate. The department states none of the 1,011 misread alerts led to a contact or arrest. Stops from correct alerts were not reported.

ladders.cameras: 117 readers: 76 fixed at 24 sites, 11 trailer, 30 mobile
ladders.note: Alerts here are verified hits only, confirmed by an employee before a stop was authorised. Per-site figures are in the table above.

Reads are MNPD's estimate from four ten-day samples (20,479,087 reads, 13,399 hit notifications, 1,346 verified hits in the samples; 511,977 reads a day over 140 days). Alerts here are unverified hit notifications in the 40 sampled days only. Arrests are persons arrested over the whole pilot; recoveries are the 26 vehicles recovered unoccupied, on top of recoveries at arrest.

Alerts: 2,877 warrant, 1,452 stolen plate, 1,192 stolen vehicle. Of 217 cases that involved an alert: 69 cleared by arrest, 52 lead generation, 33 in progress, 31 unable to locate, 20 cleared otherwise, 7 no action.
250 incident responses attributed to the readers; 24 arrests 'directly related'. A 2021 study of the city's earlier vendor found under 0.3% of hits became leads.
29 firearms recovered. One 30-day portal window showed about 2 million vehicles and 175,916 hits. The city later ended the contract.
At least 52 arrests 'directly from' reader data plus 29 assists; about 40 vehicles. A January to June 2025 audit found no impermissible use.
Arrests are 'individuals charged' (1,985 charges). Also 43 stolen plates, 521 warrants served, 32 missing persons located, 166 firearms seized.

ladders.cameras: Fixed readers at every island entrance
ladders.note: 72 stops caused by alerts produced 40 stolen vehicles and 9 stolen plates, as reported in a 2026 essay citing the department.
The county's erroneous-hits export: 214 rows, 77% marked wrong state. Correct hits were not exported, so the denominator is unknown. Per-location rows are mapped above.
The town publishes camera sites and ten dated cases rather than counts. The council paused the cameras in 2026.

statements.text: About 700 agencies surveyed in 43 states; Flock technology 'supported' about 1 million investigations in 2025, about 20% of cleared cases; about 10,000 missing persons located. Flock's own caveat: 'directional estimates rather than audited totals'.
About 20 billion plate reads a month across the network, as stated to reporters in 2026.

statements.who: Mourtgos and Adams, working paper, August 2026
statements.text: Staggered event study of 216 Flock agencies against about 3,000 others, 2017 to 2023: vehicle theft down 11% (confidence interval 4% to 17%), theft clearances by arrest up 15.9%. Deployment dates were supplied by Flock; not peer reviewed.
More than 200 documented misuse or error incidents, including 27 wrongful stops or detentions, compiled from news and records.
